text: Large language models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on vast amounts of text from books, articles, and websites. By analyzing patterns in this data, they learn to predict the next word in a sentence, which lets them generate natural-sounding responses. When you use an LLM, you give it a prompt—a question or instruction—and the model uses its training to craft an answer. The quality of the output often depends on how clear and specific your prompt is, a skill called prompt engineering. LLMs can write essays, summarize complex ideas, or even help with coding, making them powerful tools. However, they have limits. They don’t truly understand context, so they can confidently produce false or biased information, and their knowledge only goes up to their training cutoff date.
